title: Clever trees
paragraphs: There’s nothing better than a walk in the countryside for lifting our spirits. Connecting with nature has been proven to help our mental health. For some, the best tonic is to stroll through a forest, but as we admire the trees that surround us, it’s worth knowing these trees are doing more than just being nice things to look at.

We’re already aware of the healing properties of trees – they produce oxygen and clean the air we breathe by absorbing about a quarter of all human-caused carbon dioxide emissions. Deforestation isn’t helping with this which is why so many people want to save them. But there’s more to these impressive forms of vegetation than we might think. Researchers have discovered evidence that proves they are actually intelligent.

It’s thought that trees talk and share resources right under our feet, using a fungal network. Under the ground are tree roots, and mingling among them, along with bacteria, are thousands of superfine threads of fungi, known as hyphae. And research has shown that they are all interconnected. They can help each other by sharing nutrients, and they can even warn of approaching threats. Scientists say it’s like the trees are talking to one another.

Ecologist Suzanne Simard has called this network the Wood Wide Web. She discovered that parent trees use this network to help their offspring. Speaking to the BBC, she said: “We found that the parent trees would favour those seedlings that were of their own kin versus the strangers” by sending them more nutrients. She also found that trees are smart enough to change their behaviour and have managed to adapt and survive in a changing environment.
So it seems trees really are the stars of our natural world, and with around three trillion of them on our planet, it’s time to show them some respect if we want them to flourish.

vocabulary.entry: tonic /ˈtɒnɪk/ n. 使人精神振作的东西；补药
vocabulary.example: A cup of hot drink is a comforting tonic on a cold winter's day.
vocabulary.translation: 一杯热饮是寒冷冬日里的一剂暖心良方。

vocabulary.example: We like to stroll along the riverbank at weekends.
vocabulary.translation: 我们喜欢在周末沿着河边漫步。

vocabulary.entry: healing property /ˈhiːlɪŋ ˈprɒpəti/ n. 疗愈功效
vocabulary.example: The healing property of this herb has been confirmed by research.
vocabulary.translation: 这种草药的疗愈功效已经被研究证实。

vocabulary.example: A sponge can absorb water quickly.
vocabulary.translation: 海绵能迅速吸收水分。

vocabulary.entry: carbon dioxide emission /ˈkɑːbən daɪˈɒksaɪd ɪˈmɪʃn/ n. 二氧化碳排放
vocabulary.example: Factories need to reduce carbon dioxide emission to protect the environment.
vocabulary.translation: 工厂需要减少二氧化碳排放以保护环境。

vocabulary.entry: deforestation /ˌdiːˌfɒrɪˈsteɪʃn/ n. 毁林；森林砍伐
vocabulary.example: Deforestation can lead to a decline in biodiversity.
vocabulary.translation: 毁林会导致生物多样性下降。

vocabulary.example: The vegetation in this area has withered due to drought.
vocabulary.translation: 这片区域的植被因干旱而枯萎。

vocabulary.entry: fungal network /ˈfʌŋɡl ˈnetwɜːk/ n. 真菌网络
vocabulary.example: The fungal network is a channel for trees to transmit information.
vocabulary.translation: 真菌网络是树木之间传递信息的通道。

vocabulary.example: The root of this tree goes deep into the soil.
vocabulary.translation: 这棵树的根部深深扎入土壤中。

vocabulary.example: The fragrance of flowers mingles with the smell of soil in the air.
vocabulary.translation: 花香与泥土的气息在空气中交织。

vocabulary.example: This bacterium is harmless to human health.
vocabulary.translation: 这种细菌对人体健康无害。

vocabulary.entry: superfine thread /ˌsuːpəˈfaɪn θred/ n. 超细丝线
vocabulary.example: This fabric is woven from superfine threads and feels soft.
vocabulary.translation: 这种面料由超细丝线织成，触感柔软。

vocabulary.example: A hypha is one of the vegetative organs of a fungus.
vocabulary.translation: 菌丝是真菌的营养器官之一。

vocabulary.example: These computers are interconnected via a network.
vocabulary.translation: 这些电脑通过网络相互连接。

vocabulary.example: Nutrients in the soil can promote plant growth.
vocabulary.translation: 土壤中的养分能促进植物生长。

vocabulary.entry: warn of /wɔːn ɒv/ 预警；提醒注意
vocabulary.example: The weather station issued a warning to warn of the approaching heavy rain.
vocabulary.translation: 气象站发布预警，提醒人们注意即将到来的暴雨。

vocabulary.example: Climate change poses a serious threat to many species.
vocabulary.translation: 气候变化对许多物种构成了严重威胁。

vocabulary.example: This ecologist is committed to studying forest ecosystems.
vocabulary.translation: 这位生态学家致力于研究森林生态系统。

vocabulary.entry: wood wide web /wʊd waɪd web/ n. 森林万维网
vocabulary.example: The wood wide web is a secret network for communication between trees.
vocabulary.translation: 森林万维网是树木之间交流的秘密网络。

vocabulary.entry: parent tree /ˈpeərənt triː/ n. 母树
vocabulary.example: The parent tree transports nutrients to seedlings through the fungal network.
vocabulary.translation: 母树会通过真菌网络向幼苗输送养分。

vocabulary.example: This bird takes good care of its offspring.
vocabulary.translation: 这只鸟悉心照料自己的后代。

vocabulary.example: Teachers should not favour any particular student.
vocabulary.translation: 老师不应该偏爱任何一个学生。

vocabulary.example: The gardener transplanted these seedlings carefully.
vocabulary.translation: 园丁小心翼翼地移栽这些幼苗。

vocabulary.example: Animals usually tend to help their own kin.
vocabulary.translation: 动物通常会更倾向于帮助自己的同类。

vocabulary.entry: flourish /ˈflʌrɪʃ/ v. 茁壮成长；繁荣发展
vocabulary.example: Plants will flourish under suitable climatic conditions.
vocabulary.translation: 在适宜的气候条件下，植物会茁壮成长。

sentences.english: There’s nothing better than a walk in the countryside for lifting our spirits.
sentences.chinese: 没什么比在乡间散步更能让人心情舒畅的了。

sentences.english: Connecting with nature has been proven to help our mental health.
sentences.chinese: 事实证明，亲近自然有助于改善我们的心理健康。

sentences.english: For some, the best tonic is to stroll through a forest, but as we admire the trees that surround us, it’s worth knowing these trees are doing more than just being nice things to look at.
sentences.chinese: 对有些人来说，最好的“良药”就是在林间漫步，但当我们欣赏着身边的树木时，或许值得了解的是，这些树木的作用远不止赏心悦目那么简单。

sentences.english: We’re already aware of the healing properties of trees – they produce oxygen and clean the air we breathe by absorbing about a quarter of all human-caused carbon dioxide emissions.
sentences.chinese: 我们早已知道树木具有有益健康的功效——它们产生氧气，还能吸收人类活动排放的约四分之一的二氧化碳，净化我们呼吸的空气。

sentences.english: Deforestation isn’t helping with this which is why so many people want to save them.
sentences.chinese: 毁林行为会破坏这一过程，这也是许多人希望保护树木的原因。

sentences.english: But there’s more to these impressive forms of vegetation than we might think.
sentences.chinese: 但这些令人赞叹的植物，远比我们想象的要“厉害”。

sentences.english: Researchers have discovered evidence that proves they are actually intelligent.
sentences.chinese: 研究人员已经找到证据，证明树木其实是有“智慧”的。

sentences.english: It’s thought that trees talk and share resources right under our feet, using a fungal network.
sentences.chinese: 人们认为，树木会通过地下的真菌网络“交谈”并共享资源。

sentences.english: Under the ground are tree roots, and mingling among them, along with bacteria, are thousands of superfine threads of fungi, known as hyphae.
sentences.chinese: 地下遍布树根，而在树根之间，除了细菌之外，还生长着成千上万条极其纤细的真菌丝，也就是菌丝。

sentences.english: And research has shown that they are all interconnected.
sentences.chinese: 研究表明，这些菌丝相互连接成网。

sentences.english: They can help each other by sharing nutrients, and they can even warn of approaching threats.
sentences.chinese: 树木可以通过这个网络共享养分，甚至还能预警即将到来的威胁。

sentences.english: Scientists say it’s like the trees are talking to one another.
sentences.chinese: 科学家称，这就像是树木之间在互相“交流”。

sentences.english: Ecologist Suzanne Simard has called this network the Wood Wide Web.
sentences.chinese: 生态学家苏珊娜·西玛德将这个网络命名为“森林万维网”。

sentences.english: She discovered that parent trees use this network to help their offspring.
sentences.chinese: 她发现，母树会通过这个网络帮助自己的后代。

sentences.english: Speaking to the BBC, she said: “We found that the parent trees would favour those seedlings that were of their own kin versus the strangers” by sending them more nutrients.
sentences.chinese: 在接受BBC采访时，她表示：“我们发现，母树会更偏向于给自己的同类幼苗输送更多养分，而非陌生的幼苗。”

sentences.english: She also found that trees are smart enough to change their behaviour and have managed to adapt and survive in a changing environment.
sentences.chinese: 她还发现，树木十分“聪明”，能够改变自身行为，从而适应不断变化的环境并存活下来。

sentences.english: So it seems trees really are the stars of our natural world, and with around three trillion of them on our planet, it’s time to show them some respect if we want them to flourish.
sentences.chinese: 如此看来，树木确实是自然界中的“明星”。地球上大约有3万亿棵树，若想让它们茁壮成长，我们是时候给予它们应有的尊重了。
